classification.difficultyReason: Move each vertex two 45-degree divisions clockwise on its existing circle, then label and join the images using the taught circular-grid method.

content.prompt: Rotate the triangle $ABC$ by $90^\circ$ clockwise about $O$.

spec.description: Editable square circular grid with five concentric circles and rays spaced 45 degrees apart. The labelled triangle prevents use of a blank-grid template. Blue distinguishes the original figure; the red point marks O.
spec.mathematics: Relative radial positions: A has radius 2 on the southwest ray; B has radius 4 on the west ray; C has radius 4 on the northwest ray. Radial indices describe grid positions, not printed numerical measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original triangle and supplied scaffold are visible.

answer.short: $A'$ is on the second circle northwest of $O$; $B'$ is on the fourth circle directly above $O$; $C'$ is on the fourth circle northeast of $O$. Join $A'B'C'$.
answer.worked: Move each vertex two $45^\circ$ divisions clockwise, keeping it on the same circle centred at $O$. Thus $A$ moves from southwest to northwest, $B$ from west to north, and $C$ from northwest to northeast. Label the images $A'$, $B'$ and $C'$, then join them.

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise question 3; answer evidence PDF page 57
spec.description: Complete circular scaffold with original blue triangle and its red clockwise quarter-turn image.
spec.mathematics: A' lies at radius 2 northwest, B' at radius 4 north, and C' at radius 4 northeast. Every vertex retains its distance from O and turns 90 degrees clockwise.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed image appears only in answer editions.
